Question: What is a general purpose microprocessor?
Answer: All Microprocessors are General Purpose only. There is a difference between Processor and Microprocessor. General Purpose Processor is called Microprocessor. Special Purpose Processors are called with the Purpose Name like Graphic Processor, Signal Processor, Math Processor, etc. Now let us discuss what Microprocessor does. It can do some functions like Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication, Division, etc. Generally Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU) does all the function. The Microprocessor also has small memory inside called as Registers. The ALU inside Microprocessor read the numbers from Register process them and store the results in Registers. What operation to be performed is given by the Programmer in a sequence of steps which is called Program. Let us understand this through an example There Registers (Internal Memory) are named as R0, R1, R2, R3, etc. MOV R0,55 -> Moving value 55 into Register R0. MOV R1,45 -> Moving value 45 into Register R1 ADD R1,R2,R3 -> R1 + R2 -> R3. Since it does general computing we call the Microprocessor as a General Purpose Processor or General Purpose Microprocessor.
